claims.claim: AlertDialog never closes from a backdrop press or an Escape keypress, unlike Dialog; it still closes on a native request-close because cancelOnRequestClose defaults to true.
claims.specTest: ADLG-01: AlertDialog never closes from backdrop press or Escape, but an explicit action closes it
claims.observed: Escape and a backdrop press both left the AlertDialog open; pressing the explicit AlertDialogCancel closed it. The Escape-never-dismisses and backdrop-never-dismisses parts of the claim are directly web-testable; the native-request-close path (Android hardware back / iOS native modal dismissal) is out of scope for a browser run and is covered by Phase 11 Part A instead.

claims.claim: Supplying open without onOpenChange warns in development and falls back to dismissable behavior.
claims.specTest: DLG-01: open without onOpenChange warns in development and falls back to dismissable behavior
claims.observed: Mounting <Dialog open={true}> with no onOpenChange logged exactly the documented dev warning ("BeeUI Dialog: `open` requires `onOpenChange`. Falling back to dismissable uncontrolled behavior."), and a subsequent Escape keypress closed it, confirming the uncontrolled fallback.

claims.claim: Backdrop press, Web Escape, and Android hardware back all route through one close policy, while dismissOnRequestClose={false}/dismissOnEscape={false} opt individual channels out.
claims.specTest: DLG-02: backdrop press and Escape route through one close policy; dismissOnEscape opts Escape out independently
claims.observed: A default Dialog closed on both Escape and a backdrop press. A dismissOnEscape={false} Dialog ignored Escape but still closed on a backdrop press, confirming the two are independent channels within the same close policy. The Android-hardware-back channel is native-only and is covered by Phase 11 Part A instead.

claims.claim: A duplicate SelectItem value disables every item sharing it and warns in development.
claims.specTest: SEL-01: a duplicate SelectItem value disables every item sharing it and warns in development
claims.observed: Two SelectItems sharing value="dup" both rendered aria-disabled="true" (a third, unique-value item did not); pressing a disabled duplicate did not select it. Console logged the documented dev warning ("BeeUI Select: duplicate option value `dup` detected. All options with that value are disabled until the duplicate is removed.").

claims.claim: Removing the selected option does not synthesize a value change - SelectValue falls back to its placeholder until a matching item returns.
claims.specTest: SEL-02: removing the selected option does not synthesize a value change; SelectValue falls back to its placeholder
claims.observed: With the parent's controlled value="keep" pointing at a SelectItem, removing that item from the rendered list flipped SelectValue's text from the item's label to the placeholder ("No selection"), while the parent's own value/readout (updated only by onValueChange) stayed "keep" - confirming no synthesized onValueChange call.

claims.claim: Dismissal (backdrop press, swipe, Web Escape, Android hardware back) routes through the same dismissOnRequestClose/onRequestClose contract Dialog uses.
claims.specTest: SHEET-01: Sheet dismissal routes through the same dismissOnRequestClose contract Dialog uses
claims.observed: A default Sheet closed on both Escape and a backdrop press, matching Dialog's default. A dismissOnRequestClose={false} Sheet ignored both Escape and a backdrop press, and only the explicit SheetClose button closed it - matching the documented contract exactly. The swipe-gesture and Android-hardware-back channels are native-only (sheet.web.tsx has no drag gesture per ADR-006) and are covered by Phase 11 Part A instead.

claims.claim: Toasts queue FIFO with at most three visible at once.
claims.specTest: TOAST-01: toasts queue FIFO with at most three visible at once
claims.observed: Enqueuing 5 toasts (Toast 1..5) via useToast().show() left exactly the 3 oldest (Toast 1-3) visible, not the 3 newest. Dismissing the oldest (Toast 1) admitted the next queued toast (Toast 4), keeping the visible set at {Toast 2, Toast 3, Toast 4} - confirming FIFO admission order with TOAST_MAX_VISIBLE=3.

claims.claim: An explicit persistent mode opts a toast out of auto-dismiss, and action-triggered dismissal is deterministic (never racing the auto-dismiss timer).
claims.specTest: TOAST-02: an explicit persistent toast never auto-dismisses; action-triggered dismissal is deterministic
claims.observed: A duration:'persistent' toast was still visible 5.5s after TOAST_DEFAULT_DURATION (5000ms) elapsed. A duration:1500 toast with an action (dismissOnPress: true) was dismissed by pressing its action button, removed exactly once, and did not reappear after waiting past its original duration - with zero console/page errors, confirming the cancelled timer never fires a redundant dismiss.
